title: Design
body:
[[software development]]
[[Paradigms]]

The [[SDLC]] phase between requirements and implementation: given what the system must do,
decide how it will be structured. Requirements are about the problem and are the customer's
to confirm; design is about the solution and is yours.

The design decision that matters is **where the boundaries go**, because everything else
follows from it. Two ways to draw them, and that is what [[Paradigms]] is about:
[[Structured Approach]] splits by function, [[Object Oriented Approach]] splits by thing.
Either way the target is the same pair: low coupling between modules, high cohesion within
them. See [[Coupling and Cohesion]].

What a good design is actually optimising for is not the first release. It is the
[[SDLC]] maintenance phase, where most of a system's life is spent. The question to ask of a
design is "when this requirement changes, how many modules do I have to open", and
[[Complexity]] is the name for the answer getting worse.

Two levels the course separates:

- **Architectural design**: the modules and how they talk. [[Microservices]] is one answer.
- **Detailed design**: the inside of each module, its data structures and algorithms, which
  is where [[INFORMATION STRUCTURES]] takes over.

[[Code Smells]] are what you see later when this phase went wrong.
